protocol.description:
Use this protocol to get a list of opened toplevels for the current seat, get their titles and app_ids, and activate or close them.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is experimental and backward incompatible changes may be made. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes are done by bumping the version number in the protocol and interface names and resetting the version number at the end. Once the protocol is to be declared stable, the 'z' prefix and the version number in the protocol and interface names are removed and the version number inside the interface is reset to 1.

interface.name: zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1
interface.description: This interface is used to request the toplevels of the current seat.

event.name: toplevel
event.description:
This event is emitted whenever a new toplevel window is created. It is emitted for all toplevels, regardless of the app that has created them.
All initial state of the toplevel will be sent immediately after this event using the usual events that are used to notify toplevel state.

request.name: stop
request.description:
This request indicates that the client no longer wishes to receive events for new toplevels.
However the compositor may emit further toplevel_created or toplevel_destroyed events, until the toplevel_finished event is emitted.
The client must not send any more requests after this one.

interface.name: zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1
interface.description: A zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 object represents an opened toplevel window. A single app may have multiple opened toplevels.

request.name: set_maximized

description.summary: requests that the toplevel be maximized

request.description: Requests that the toplevel be maximized. If the maximized state actually changes, the compositor will send a state event.

request.name: unset_maximized

description.summary: requests that the toplevel be unmaximized

request.description: Requests that the toplevel be unmaximized. If the maximized state actually changes, the compositor will send a state event.

request.name: set_minimized

description.summary: requests that the tooplevel be minimized

request.description: Requests that the toplevel be minimized. If the minimized state actually changes, the compositor will send a state event.

request.name: unset_minimized

description.summary: requests that the toplevel be unminimized

request.description: Requests that the toplevel be unminimized. If the minimized state actually changes, the compositor will send a state event.

request.name: activate
request.description: Request that this toplevel be activated on the given seat after wl_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1.stop is called. There is no guarantee that the request will be fulfilled; the compositor may ignore it.

request.name: close
request.description: Request that this toplevel be closed. This is only a request that the window should be closed, the client may ignore it.

request.name: set_rectangle
request.description:
The rectangle of the surface specified in this request is a hint for the compositor to place the popup menus of the client (such as context menus) near the toplevel.
The x and y coordinates are relative to the surface, and the rectangle is in the same coordinate space as the toplevel.

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Destroys the zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 object. This request should be called when the client is no longer interested in the toplevel, or when the toplevel has been closed.
After this request, the client must not send any more requests on this object.

event.name: title
event.description:
The title of the toplevel has changed.
The configured state may not be applied immediately; a state event will be sent once the new state is applied.

event.name: app_id
event.description:
The app id of the toplevel has changed.
The app id is a stable identifier for the application, usually the desktop entry name (e.g. "org.kde.kate"). The compositor may use it to find the application icon.

event.name: output_enter
event.description: This event is emitted whenever the toplevel becomes visible on the given output. A toplevel may be visible on multiple outputs.

event.name: output_leave
event.description: This event is emitted whenever the toplevel stops being visible on the given output.

event.name: state
event.description:
This event is emitted immediately after the zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 is created and each time the toplevel state changes, either because of a compositor action or because of a request in this protocol.
The initial state is empty, and the state is empty when the toplevel is closed; the state is empty until the closed event is emitted.

event.name: done

description.summary: all information about the toplevel has been sent

event.description:
This event is sent after all changes in the toplevel state have been sent.
This allows changes to the zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 properties to be seen as atomic, even if they happen via multiple events.

event.name: closed
event.description:
The server has destroyed the toplevel and the zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 object is now inert.
The client should destroy this object.

event.name: parent
event.description:
The parent of the toplevel has been set or unset.
This event is sent after the parent is set or unset, and the client should update the toplevel hierarchy accordingly.
